 Order

This is fifth bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, for grant of bail relating to FIR/Crime No.50/2022 dated 07.02.2023 registered at Police Station- Garh, District Rewa, for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366 and 376(3) of Indian Penal Code and Section 3, 4 of POCSO Act.
2. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in custody since 07.02.2023 and the trial will take considerable time to conclude.
He further submits that the applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.

The applicant is the permanent resident of district and Mohd. Abid Khan @ Monu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43249488/
1 there is no possibility of his absconding or tampering with prosecution evidence.

sentences.text: He is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the conditions to be imposed by the Court.
Upon these grounds, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
3. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection.

4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
5.

Vide order dated 10.01.2024, the applicant was directed to submit documents showing arrangements that have been made or were earlier made for the ceremony of marriage of his sister,
but counsel for applicant has submitted that he has already filed the invitation card and the certificate and no further documents can be submitted.
It has also been requested that on the basis of these documents, the order may be passed.
6. It appears that the ground of marriage of sister is being taken repeatedly by the applicant without filing documents relating to arrangement of ceremony.
Merely on the basis of invitation card, it cannot be inferred that the marriage is scheduled to be arranged on 21.01.2024.
Particularly in the light of fact that earlier this marriage was scheduled to be organized in the first week of December and later in 4th/5th week of December, 2023.
7. Regular bail application of the applicant, who is facing the accusation of rape and POCSO Act, has already been dismissed vide order dated 09.10.2023 under M.Cr.C. No.34474/2023.

It is rather surprising that despite arrangements of marriage on three occasions the applicant has not been in a position to file any document regarding those arrangements and on every occasion he has only submitted the invitation card.
Surprisingly, the marriage is to be solemnized in near future and still no payments are shown to have been made.
Non-availability of documents relating to arrangements made for the ceremony itself reflects the absence of truth in the claim.
8. Looking to these facts, this Court does not find it appropriate to release the applicant on bail.
9. Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands dismissed.

(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE pnm Date: 2024.01.17 18:15:40 +05'30'
